model.scope: Financial sensitivity model using real service/shop/settlement/repair quotes. Survival, loot value, protection spent, acquisition chances and durations are assumptions, not measured human results. This does not establish progression balance, strategy dominance or a viable exploit. Quest progression, XP utility, combat benefits and player enjoyment are not reduced to a credit rate.

assumptions.paidSupplies: One bought medium-ammo pack plus one field medkit per attempt. The pack is consumed/lost before the outcome; the weapon starts/finishes a surviving attempt with its original magazine capacity.
assumptions.loot: Sale value of recovered loot after capacity/quest rules. Equal values across strategies are controlled comparisons, not a claim that gear/capacity gives no advantage.
assumptions.insurance: Optimistic eventual return value of eligible unclaimed equipment. Return delay, raid closure, replacement cash/backup gear, destruction and stock shortages can make actual affordability worse.
assumptions.materials: Market replacement or foregone resale, shown separately; no assumption of free repair materials.
assumptions.stock: Expected hourly purchase demand is compared with fresh account stock. Loot, alternative weapon classes, batch restock timing and delayed insurance availability are not simulated.
assumptions.oneTimeCosts: Starter allowance and unlock delays are excluded from steady-state net income. Station upgrade transactions/material costs are quoted separately and are not automatically amortized into those rows.
assumptions.protectedRush: Capacity-only maxima sampled from all caches, including gated/dangerous areas. Assumed access chances and two-minute attempts are deliberately varied. No route, survival rate or profitable human strategy has been demonstrated.

scenario.impairment: application-level request/response loss and injected delay over loopback HTTP; not packet-level WAN loss

economy.scope: Client-observed wallet deltas and stash sale quotes from authenticated APIs. Final balances may include active raids; stash quotes exclude deployed/overflow equipment, attachments and future insurance. Returned bring-in items are not counted as newly recovered loot. Phase attribution is observational, not the server audit ledger. Conservation checks validate observer arithmetic, not fraud resistance.

limits: No gameplay prices or protected rules were changed; the model is sensitivity analysis, not player balance acceptance.
Fixed full-kit replacement differs from the live mixed-strategy pilot, which uses available gear and falls back to recovery.
Protected pool ceilings ignore access/travel/competition; a dedicated rushing strategy must be measured before asserting dominance.
Insurance return timing, stock availability, equipment reuse and upfront resource pack cash affect real affordability.
One-time contract rewards and remaining starter support must not be extrapolated as indefinitely recurring income.
All nine players ended with active equipment, so final stash/credit totals are not total wealth.
The older two-hour soak loaded different source and has no economy observer; it remains separate evidence.
Full feature completion is still unproven in RELEASE_ACCEPTANCE.md.
